He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]], who [[retired number|retired]] his jersey. ==Early life== Singletary was born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]. He attended C. W. Henry Elementary School in [[Mount Airy, Philadelphia]], attended [[The Haverford School]] and then [[The Perkiomen School]] for his freshman and sophomore years of high school, then attended high school at [[William Penn Charter School]] in Philadelphia for his junior and senior years. He was also a [[American football|football]] player in high school, excelling at [[wide receiver]], but he gave up the sport to focus on basketball. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Singletary was listed as the No. 10 point guard and the No. 56 player in the nation in 2004.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Sean-Singletary-12920;_ylt=ArtSgYfQaFK8b45l2Gu_AgHXO5B4 Sean Singletary Recruiting Profile] ==College career== Singletary improved upon his All-ACC Freshman performance in 2004–05 by averaging 17.7 points per game and earning all-ACC first team honors during his sophomore season, which included his second highest scoring game, a 35-point effort against an [[Adam Morrison]]-led [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] team. Singletary was Virginia's floor leader during their pivotal 2006–07 season in which the team moved from their old home at [[University Hall (University of Virginia)|University Hall]] across the street to the 130 million dollar [[John Paul Jones Arena]]. Virginia enjoyed perhaps its best season since 1994–95 with Singletary and senior [[J.R. Reynolds|J. R. Reynolds]]. On March 9, 2008, against the University of Maryland, Singletary scored his 2,000th career point and finished the game with 2,002 points, and finished his career as the fifth-highest all-time scorer in school history with 2,079 points. He also joined greats Greivis Vasquéz, Johnny Dawkins, and Danny Ferry as the only four players in ACC history to record 2,000 career points, 500 career assists, and 400 career rebounds; adding his 200 career steals makes him the only ACC player to ever record each of those four milestones. Singletary was selected to the 2007–08 All-ACC team, making him, [[Bryant Stith]], and [[Ralph Sampson]] the only three Cavaliers to be named all-conference three times in their careers. Singletary's number 44 was retired by the University of Virginia at halftime of a game against [[Clemson Tigers|Clemson]] on February 15, 2009.[http://www.virginiasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=88843&SPID=10616&DB_OEM_ID=17800&ATCLID=3658207|Sean Singletary's Number to be Retired] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327074419/http://www.virginiasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=88843&SPID=10616&DB_OEM_ID=17800&ATCLID=3658207%7CSean |date=2012-03-27 }} As a freshman, he was the only player on the team to start every game during the 2004–2005 season, and was selected to the All-Atlantic Coast Conference Freshman Team. He averaged 10.5 points per game, as well as 3.9 assists per contest in his [[rookie]] campaign. Singletary ranked first among [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] freshmen in assists and steals, second in minutes played and third in scoring. He was selected to the CollegeInsider.com Freshmen All-America Team and a second-team selection to the Rivals.com Freshmen All-America Team. In his sophomore year, Singletary earned a first team All-Atlantic Coast Conference selection (the first from UVA since [[Bryant Stith]] in '92) by averaging 17.7 points (1st team, 5th ACC), and ranking third in FT% in the ACC (.845 125–148), fifth in steals (1.86 54), and sixth in assists (4.17 apg. 121). Against [[Gonzaga University|Gonzaga]] on December 17, 2005, he scored a career-high 35 points, including four 3-pointers, and had six steals and six rebounds in an 11-point loss,[https://web.archive.org/web/20121008184255/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=253512250 Morrison, Gonzaga hand Virginia third straight loss] and was named ACC Player of The Week. His first career double-double (29 pts, 10 reb) came in the [[ACC Tournament]] against the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]] on March 10, 2006.[https://web.archive.org/web/20121008184312/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=260690153 No. 10 Tar Heels ice Virginia to reach ACC semis] Singletary was also a co-captain of the Cavaliers and was also named First-team All-ACC selection by SI.com, State Player of the Year and a first-team All-State selection by the VaSID, Player of the Year in Virginia and first-team All-State as selected by the ''[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]'', co-recipient of the [[Bill Gibson (basketball)|Bill Gibson]] Cavalier of the Year Award (team MVP), co-recipient of the Sidney Young Memorial Trophy (team award to that athlete who exemplifies the highest qualities of leadership, cooperative spirit and unselfish service in the interest of athletics at the University of Virginia), and received the team's Most Assists Award. Singletary became one of the elite point guards in the country his junior year, scoring in double digits in all but one game.[http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=22208&year=2007 2006-2007 Season Sean Singletary Game Log]{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} He finished the season first on his team and third in the ACC in scoring with 19.0 points per game. Although Virginia started the season slowly, Singletary was instrumental in a seven game in-conference win streak that helped Virginia win a share of the ACC regular season title with an 11–5 record. On January 3, 2007, he scored a career-high 37 points in a blowout of [[Gonzaga University|Gonzaga]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20121008184321/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270030258 Virginia 108, Gonzaga 87] Singletary gained national attention when he hit an acrobatic game-winning shot against [[Duke University|Duke]] on February 1, 2007, with 1.0 seconds left on the clock, giving Virginia a win over Duke 68–66.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120714224439/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270320258|title=Virginia uses late shot to level No. 10 Duke in OT}} On March 6, 2007, Singletary was named to the first team All-Atlantic Coast Conference team for the second consecutive season and was named as a third team All-American by the National Association of Basketball coaches. Along with backcourt mate J.R. Reynolds, he led UVA to its first [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] berth since 2001, where they played the [[University of Albany]] in the first round. Singletary scored 23 points and had 9 assists in a 27-point win over UAlbany.[https://web.archive.org/web/20070319182043/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000036 One-two punch of Reynolds, Singletary key UVA win] In the second round, Singletary scored 19 points, but only shot 29% from the floor and missed the potential game tying shot in a 77–74 loss to [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20070320201849/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000037 Vols overcome strong guard play by UVA to reach Sweet 16] After his missed shot, Singletary fell to the ground crying. Seconds later his coach and teammates approached him to offer consolation. Singletary confirmed to head coach [[Dave Leitao]] that he would return for his senior year season just hours before the 5 p.m. draft withdrawal deadline. For the 2007–08 season, Singletary was Virginia's primary offensive weapon. Singletary was a co-captain of the 2007–08 Cavaliers, along with Adrian Joseph. Singletary was among conference leaders in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] in several statistical categories. As of late February he was second in the ACC in assists, third in scoring, ninth in steals and third in free throw percentage. He had his highest scoring game on March 1, 2008, against Miami, when he scored 41 points.[https://web.archive.org/web/20080307065550/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280612390 Miami 95, Virginia 93] Singletary was selected to the 2007–2008 1st Team All ACC for the third consecutive year. His last collegiate basketball game was a loss against [[Bradley University]] at home, in the [[College Basketball Invitational]] Tournament. He scored 17 points in the game and received a standing ovation from his loyal fans for his legendary career as a Cavalier.[https://web.archive.org/web/20121008184532/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280860258 Bradley 96, Virginia 85] ==Professional career == After undergoing offseason hip surgery, Sean Singletary was selected in the second round of the [[2008 NBA draft]] with the 42nd pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. In August 2008 he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] along with [[Patrick Ewing Jr.]] and [[Ron Artest]] (now [[Metta World Peace]]){{cite web |title=It's official: Rockets acquire Ron Artest in blockbuster trade |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/Itrsquos_official_Ron_Artes-280197-34.html |date=2008-08-21 |accessdate=2009-01-19}} then subsequently traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[D. J. Strawberry]].{{cite web |title=Suns Acquire Sean Singletary |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/singletary_080825.html |accessdate=2008-12-11}} On December 10, 2008, he was traded once again along with [[Boris Diaw]] and [[Raja Bell]] to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for [[Jason Richardson]] and [[Jared Dudley]].{{cite web |title=Bobcats Acquire Boris Diaw, Raja Bell and Sean Singletary from Phoenix |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/081210_bobcats_trade.html |date=2008-12-10 |accessdate=2008-12-11 |url-status=dead along with [[Alexis Ajinça]] to the [[NBA D-League]]'s [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web |title=Bobcats Assign Ajinca and Singletary to D-League Affiliate |work=[[NBA.com]] |archive-date=2012-05-31 |date=2009-07-03 |accessdate=2009-07-03}} He signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in September 2009,[http://www.philly.com/inquirer/sports/20090929_Four_hopefuls_eye_spot_with_76ers.html Four hopefuls eye spot with 76ers] but was waived in October of that year.[http://www.seattlepi.com/scorecard/nbanews.asp?articleID=266166 Sixers waive Swift, Singletary]. Retrieved on October 12, 2009. On November 10, 2009, he signed with the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] team [[Saski Baskonia|Caja Laboral]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=62492 |title=El Caja Laboral ficha al base Sean Singletary |access-date=November 10, 2009 |archive-date=September 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180926124607/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=62492 |url-status=dead }} Singletary played his last game with Caja Laboral on April 17, 2010.[http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Spain/2010/0417_1993_108.asp Regular season round 30: Fuenlabrada - Caja Laboral 90-86] Caja Laboral later became the ACB champion.[http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Spain/2010/0615_108_100.asp Finals Game 3: Caja Laboral - Regal Barca 79-78 OT] In 2011–12, he played for the [[Basketball League Belgium Division I|Belgian League]] team [[Dexia Mons-Hainaut]]. On November 2, 2012, he was selected by the [[Texas Legends]] in the second round of the 2012 NBA D-League Draft.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2012/ 2012 NBA Development League Draft] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114152434/http://www.nba.com/dleague/draft2012/ |date=2016-01-14 }} He was waived by the team on April 5, 2013, due to an injury.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/transactions_201213.html 2012-13 Transactions] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131210180258/http://www.nba.com/dleague/transactions_201213.html |date=2013-12-10 }} Later that month, he joined [[BC Oostende|Telenet Oostende]] of Belgium for the rest of the 2012–13 season. In November 2013, he was re-acquired by the Texas Legends.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/legends_complete_three_trades_2013_11_04.html Legends Complete Three Trades, Finalize Training Camp Roster] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109041804/http://www.nba.com/dleague/texas/legends_complete_three_trades_2013_11_04.html |date=November 9, 2013 }} On January 22, 2014, he was traded to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/melo_orton_trade_2014_01_22.html Fab Melo, Daniel Orton Moved in Four-Team Trade] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026225648/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/melo_orton_trade_2014_01_22.html |date=2015-10-26 }} On March 26, 2014, he was waived by the BayHawks due to a season-ending injury.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_release_singletary_2014_03_26.html BayHawks Release Singletary] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328004214/http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_release_singletary_2014_03_26.html |date=2014-03-28 }} Singletary retired from basketball at the
